_note: Operator alarms (#566, Sprint 45 Track I). EVERY sentence in this file is marked for Noel's review; none is approved copy. Keys named in Astra's design of 2026-09-22 keep those names. Placeholders are named, never positional. {meter} is the radio's own label for the meter, {point} the place-phrase for a supply meter, {units} its units in words, {value} the reading, {alarm} the operator's name for the alarm.
_review_points: Where on the supply the voltage is measured, in the few words a ham says, at ONE length. RULED by Noel 2026-10-01 07:17 and 07:18 (#566): 'low supply voltage before THE fuse', and the place phrases EVERYWHERE are before the fuse, after the fuse, at the PA and at the CPU, in preset names, in the normal warning and in the terse warning alike. A terse warning is shortened by dropping the follow-up advice, never the place. This SUPERSEDES the two-lengths part of the 2026-09-23 04:42 ruling; its no-commas part stands, so no sentence that leads with a name runs into its verb. A meter we have not met is named by the radio's own meter name, after the word meter, rather than relabelled with another radio's words (Sol's language pass, 2026-10-01).
_review_warnings: The spoken warnings. The action FIRST where the alarm has one, so the first complete clause works alone if the rest is cut off, then the condition and value, then any follow-up advice. Supply warnings name low or high, so the listener never infers the direction from a number, and fall warnings keep 'from its baseline' (or 'from baseline' at terse), because the fall is measured from a captured baseline and not from the previous reading. A .terse key is the warning at Terse verbosity: the same place phrase, without the follow-up advice. The rising-fast frames keep 'now' before the value rather than 'to', because a re-read reminder carries the rise from its firing and the value from the current reading. None of them says transmit was cut, because it was not. Adopted from Sol's language pass, 2026-10-01.

_review_generic: An alarm the operator defined, or a shipped preset edited so its own words no longer hold. The action clause goes FIRST when there is one. The firing frames say 'Your alarm named ... fired' because the name is the operator's data and may no longer describe the meter after an edit, and the line carries its unit as the value does (Sol's language pass, 2026-10-01). The still_active frames are spoken when a re-read warning's CURRENT reading is inside the clear margin, where 'at or above the line' would be false of the number stated; they give the reading and what clears the alarm instead (Astra's Track IJK2 review, blocker 3; DRAFT, 2026-10-01). The _no_band pair is for an alarm with no clear margin the meter can represent, which clears only strictly past the line, so 'at or below' would promise a clearance the monitor never grants; {clear} is the line itself there (Astra's Track IJK4 review, blocker 1; DRAFT, 2026-10-01).

_review_presets: Preset names as they appear in the list and the preset picker, and in every sentence that names the alarm. Named the way a ham says them, ruled by Noel 2026-09-22 (#566) on hearing 'Delete the alarm PA temperature high?': 'Also weird. Delete the high PA temperature alarm.' The reversed order was the preset's NAME leaking through, so the name is what changed. {point} is the place-phrase for the supply meter, WITHOUT a comma (ruled 2026-09-23 04:42) and with its article (ruled 2026-10-01 07:17): a 6300 says before the fuse and after the fuse, an 8600 says at the PA and at the CPU, so 'Delete the Low supply voltage before the fuse alarm?' reads straight through. The place phrase has one length, so a name says the same place as the warning at every verbosity. An operator's own preset keeps whatever name they typed, and a definition already saved under an older name keeps its stored name — a name is not an identity.

_review_validation: Validation names the field, keeps the entered values, and puts focus on the field.
alarms.validation.name_too_long: The name is too long; keep it under eighty characters.
alarms.validation.threshold_not_finite: The line must be a number.
alarms.validation.hysteresis_not_number: The clear margin must be a number.
alarms.validation.sustained_count_not_wh: Readings in a row must be a whole number.
alarms.validation.sustained_seconds_not_: The span must be a number of seconds.
alarms.validation.freshness_not_number: The longest silence must be a number of seconds.
alarms.validation.reminder_not_number: The repeat interval must be a number of seconds.
alarms.validation.worsening_not_number: Enter a number for "Announce a further move".
alarms.validation.hysteresis_negative: The clear margin cannot be negative.
alarms.validation.freshness_not_positive: The longest silence must be more than zero seconds.
alarms.validation.sustained_invalid: Several readings in a row needs at least two, and a span of zero or more seconds.
alarms.validation.clear_invalid: Clearing needs at least one reading and a span of zero or more seconds.
alarms.validation.reminder_negative: The repeat interval cannot be negative. Zero turns repeats off.
alarms.validation.worsening_negative: Enter zero or more for "Announce a further move". Zero turns it off.
alarms.validation.clear_equals_trigger: With a clear margin, the clear line cannot be the same as the line.
alarms.validation.trend_interval_invalid: The trend timing does not add up: the window must hold both bands and the interval, and the reset rise must be below the trigger rise.
alarms.validation.out_of_range_review: The line is outside this meter's published range of {low} to {high} {units}. Save it if you mean it.
